recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-9240 unless the Security work group opens a new tracker to change Signature Type terminology policy.
issue_request: FHIR-9240 was a Published/Persuasive Security change request for DSTU2 asking that the Signature Type value set stop defining FHIR codes for a Coding element and instead use a non-FHIR code system, with the resolution saying the vocabulary should clearly be ASTM.
initial_application: Jira records SVN revision 7952 as the application. The corresponding git-svn commit 2cc1452ce1d1f421f880a81f501c3b1ad2765064 changed source/datatypes/valueset-signature-type.xml from http://hl7.org/fhir/valueset-signature-type to urn:iso-astm:E1762-95:2013.
additional_context: Current source keeps Signature as an active normative datatype, registers the ASTM and ETSI signature type CodeSystems in source/fhir.ini, and binds Signature.type to valueset-signature-type. FHIR-20807 later added ETSI commitment types to the same value set for R5 while preserving the external ASTM include, so later terminology work did not reverse FHIR-9240.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active value set already composes from urn:iso-astm:E1762-95:2013 and http://uri.etsi.org/01903/v1.2.2, and the ASTM CodeSystem source identifies ASTM as publisher with ASTM copyright text.

related_jiras.note: Added ETSI signature commitment types to the same Signature Type value set while preserving the ASTM external-code-system approach required by FHIR-9240.
